facts.raw_span: A 4-year-old girl of Turkish ancestry was brought to the emergency department for progressive unsteadiness and recurrent falls over the preceding 5 days
no prior medical history
she was alert (GCS 15), afebrile, and appeared well
Both external ear canals were obstructed by effusion and cerumen
Three-month history of “ear problems”
initial diagnosis of otitis media with effusion and tympanic perforation treated with antibiotics led to partial resolution
the left tympanic membrane was intact without effusion
the right external canal was occluded by polypoid tissue and purulent secretion
Contrast-enhanced CT of the head and temporal bones revealed bilateral osteolysis of the mastoids, superior and lateral semicircular canals, and the right external auditory canal
Brainstem evoked response audiometry demonstrated a threshold of 40 dB with normal wave latencies on the left and an 80 dB threshold with prolonged wave I latency on the right
indicating profound right-sided hearing loss
adenoid hypertrophy and mild sinus mucosal thickening
